::: {.callout-important}
## Decision

**STUDY07-R5 — EM demonstration failed.** Under the qualified `sblr` 0.2.0
defaults, neither SBayesRC-EM nor SBayesRC-S-EM reached its registered outer
convergence tolerances in 50 iterations, and both retained material dependence
on dispersed annotation starts. Downstream genomic inference was often useful,
but that does not satisfy the prespecified EM stability gate.

This is a controlled result on one frozen simulation replicate. It is not a
general calibration, scaling, or superiority claim.
:::

## Motivation

Study 06 found difficult joint exploration of learned annotation effects and
SNP allocations even when SNP-level summaries were substantially more stable.
Study 07 asks whether the separately derived MCEM inference lines remove that
practical instability on exactly the benchmark that exposed it. MCEM/MAP is
not a replacement transition for the joint posterior, and its endpoint need
not equal any individual joint chain.

## Frozen data and provenance

Exactly one pre-existing Study 06 dataset was reused: scenario
`informative_annotations`, replicate 1, with 2,000 individuals (1,400 training,
600 validation), 1,500 markers in 15 registered 100-marker blocks, and seeds
105412/105424/105438/3101/5201 for component/effect/residual/split/annotation
construction. It was selected from pre-existing evidence because it most
clearly combined learned-alpha/allocation mixing difficulty with stable useful
SNP inference; no Study 07 result informed selection.

```text
Study 06 specification: 241c15afab8fefc571e38e625130de6e4ab58b958c30cff369e26998ee30fa56
Study 06 truth:         169d52bef390022a9106d7e61b200493869b40cbb76f1c8d911eebbc80fea1eb
sblrbench source:       710047c5b53a5cb64d9bf2201c7634ac6f71bcd1
sblr source:            a85b749dfb903364c5cdb17ef8b8efc1583e347d
sblr version:           0.2.0
installed-tree SHA-256: a22927d8d1b6f7c8af3a5b18db5e7a827865832ea1f5bb47f6a4fd21ebb32b65
```

The historical repository implementation map describes `sblr` 0.1.2 and is
not authoritative here. The former Study 07 implementation was retired after
its compact scientific result and registered specification were preserved.
Gate 7 added the
registered Study 06 SBayesR mixture prior after the first infrastructure-only
baseline attempt exposed its omission. Before any selection fit, Gate 10 also
removed an accidental truth-derived delta initialization and registered the
neutral all-included start. Neither correction followed annotation-method
results.

## Methods and inference replication

The five prespecified methods were SBayesR, joint SBayesRC, SBayesRC-EM, joint
SBayesRC-S, and SBayesRC-S-EM. Joint methods used four 6,000-draw retained
chains after 3,000 burn-in iterations. EM methods used independent baseline,
positive, negative, and mixed annotation starts with their qualified defaults:
1,000 inner sweeps, 300 burn-in, damping 0.5, tolerances 0.001, and at most 50
outer iterations; S-EM additionally used 2,000/500 selection sweeps/burn-in.
These are inference diagnostics on one dataset, not new simulation replicates.

SBayesRC-EM fixed `sigmaSqAlpha`, made no independent global Pi update, learned
B/E during the outer fit, and ran a separate frozen-prior genomic block.
SBayesRC-S-EM fixed `pi_A` and `tau2`; `annotation_pip_eb` is conditional on its
final Rao-Blackwell responsibilities and is not the full joint
`annotation_pip`.

## Joint reference behavior

The Study 06 phenomenon was reproduced. Ordinary joint SBayesRC had worst raw
alpha R-hat 1.100 (minimum bulk ESS 45.8), and active occupancy had R-hat 1.038
(bulk ESS 87.3). Nevertheless, chain-mean annotation priors reconstructed from
genuine retained alpha histories were much more stable: minimum pairwise
Pearson correlation was 0.996 for full component priors and 0.969 for active
priors. Joint SBayesRC-S was similarly difficult in its weakest directions
(worst alpha R-hat 1.124; null-delta R-hat 1.051), while informative annotation
PIPs were 1.00 in every chain.

## Continuous annotation inference

| Method/start | Alpha RMSE | Alpha correlation | Prior RMSE | Prior correlation | Active-prior correlation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Joint SBayesRC | 0.468 | 0.917 | 0.048 | 0.993 | 0.908 |
| EM baseline | 0.326 | 0.895 | 0.053 | 0.990 | 0.914 |
| EM positive | 0.248 | 0.936 | 0.049 | 0.992 | 0.916 |
| EM negative | 0.375 | 0.869 | 0.062 | 0.987 | 0.847 |
| EM mixed | 0.412 | 0.824 | 0.050 | 0.992 | 0.973 |

All four SBayesRC-EM starts reached the 50-outer cap without the `converged`
flag. Their largest terminal alpha/prior deltas were 0.0156/0.0101. Endpoint
differences were material: maximum absolute between-start differences were
0.837 for `alpha_map`, 0.463 for component priors, 0.412 for active priors,
and 0.419 for final SNP PIPs. Expected active counts ranged from 141 to 208.
Minimum pairwise Pearson correlations were 0.714 for active priors and 0.838
for genomic PIPs, although posterior mean beta remained much more stable
(minimum Pearson 0.997).
High truth correlations therefore coexist with failure of the requested
start-invariance gate.

## Annotation selection

| Annotation | Truth | Joint PIP (chain range) | S-EM EB-PIP range | S-EM delta patterns (baseline/positive/negative/mixed) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| enriched binary | 1 | 1.000 (1.000–1.000) | 0.955–1.000 | 1/1/1/1 |
| continuous signal | 1 | 1.000 (1.000–1.000) | 0.007–1.000 | 0/1/1/0 |
| null annotation | 0 | 0.524 (0.327–0.687) | 0.000–1.000 | 0/0/1/1 |

All SBayesRC-S-EM starts also hit the outer cap. The maximum terminal
alpha/prior deltas were 0.181/0.0159, and `delta_map` differed by start. The
baseline selected enriched only, the positive start selected both true signals,
the negative start selected all annotations, and the mixed start selected
enriched plus null. Consequently conditional EB-PIP behavior is not stable on
this benchmark, despite one start recovering the binary truth pattern.
Across S-EM starts, active-prior and genomic-PIP minimum Pearson correlations
were 0.528 and 0.759, whereas posterior mean beta again compressed much of the
difference (minimum Pearson 0.983).

## Genomic inference

| Method | Beta correlation | Beta RMSE | PIP Brier | Expected active | Validation prediction correlation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| SBayesR | 0.860 | 0.0133 | 0.0900 | 176.8 | 0.603 |
| Joint SBayesRC | 0.886 | 0.0121 | 0.0729 | 125.1 | 0.632 |
| SBayesRC-EM starts | 0.885–0.888 | 0.0120–0.0121 | 0.0732–0.0768 | 140.9–207.7 | 0.630–0.633 |
| Joint SBayesRC-S | 0.886 | 0.0121 | 0.0726 | 122.5 | 0.632 |
| SBayesRC-S-EM starts | 0.871–0.889 | 0.0119–0.0128 | 0.0731–0.0875 | 128.9–162.0 | 0.612–0.631 |

Annotation methods generally improved beta/PIP recovery over SBayesR, and most
EM endpoints retained useful genomic inference. This downstream utility does
not erase the start dependence: maximum between-start genomic-PIP differences
were 0.419 for continuous EM and 0.645 for S-EM.

The true global B/E values are approximately 0.0255/1.000. Block-route B
summaries were on the expected scale (SBayesR 0.0231, joint SBayesRC 0.0283;
continuous-EM final genomic summaries 0.0225–0.0239). Their reported E was
about 1.988 and derived h2 about 0.33, reproducing the known retained-block
variance context rather than resolving it. The qualified CSR joint-selection
route has a different global residual contract and gave B/E 0.0287/0.982 with
h2 0.504; these values are not evidence that its posterior is identical to the
block methods. Outer-fit B endpoints varied by start (0.0190–0.0295 for
continuous EM; 0.0177–0.0356 for S-EM), while E remained 1.9879.

## Runtime and figures

Joint wall times were 33.5 seconds (SBayesR), 25.4 seconds (SBayesRC), and 32.7
seconds (SBayesRC-S). Continuous-EM starts took 186–286 seconds and S-EM starts
took 182–238 seconds. Local deterministic outputs include seven compact CSVs
and four figures:

```text
results/local/07_joint_em_sbayesrc/tables/
results/local/07_joint_em_sbayesrc/figures/annotation_stability.png
results/local/07_joint_em_sbayesrc/figures/active_prior_truth.png
results/local/07_joint_em_sbayesrc/figures/genomic_beta_truth.png
results/local/07_joint_em_sbayesrc/figures/annotation_selection.png
```

They remain ignored working evidence. No capsule was promoted before scientific
review.

## Conclusion and stop decision

The one-replicate result is clear enough to stop: under current qualified
defaults, the EM lines did **not** demonstrate stable annotation inference from
dispersed starts on the Study 06 benchmark. Useful genomic inference survived
in many endpoints, echoing Study 06's separation between hierarchy-level and
SNP-level stability, but the primary EM gate failed. No additional simulation
replicate, retuning grid, or model-development run is warranted inside this
study. Any follow-up should first be a focused `sblr` method-development audit
of outer convergence/start dependence on this frozen case, outside
`sblrbench` Study 07.
